plain.headline: A Holy Home
plain.intro: Today the Church looks at Jesus growing up in a real family with Mary and Joseph. Sirach teaches children to honor and care for their parents, and Paul describes a home built on patience, forgiveness, and love. In the Gospel, Mary and Joseph bring the baby Jesus to the Temple, where two faithful old people recognize him as the Savior.
plain.listen: what Simeon says when he holds the child in his arms

Reading 1.box: Sirach teaches that honoring your father and mother pleases God and brings blessing. He asks grown children to be patient and kind with parents who become old and weak. Sirach was a Jewish teacher in Jerusalem who wrote about two hundred years before Christ.

chunks.text: The Lord gives a father honor over his children, and he upholds a mother's authority over her sons. Whoever honors his father makes up for his sins. Whoever respects his mother is like someone storing up treasure.

Whoever honors his father will find joy in his own children, and God will hear him when he prays. Whoever respects his father will have a long life. Whoever obeys the Lord brings comfort to his mother.

My child, take care of your father when he is old, and do not make him sad as long as he lives. If his mind begins to fail, be patient with him. Do not look down on him while you are strong. Kindness to your father will not be forgotten. It will count for you against your sins and build up your life.

Responsorial Psalm.box: The psalm sings of the happiness of anyone who honors God and follows his ways. Their work bears fruit, and their home is full of life, with children gathered around the table like young olive trees.

Reading 2.box: Paul tells the Christians of Colossae how God's chosen people should live together: with kindness, patience, forgiveness, and above all love. He then speaks to wives, husbands, children, and fathers in turn. Each of these duties is meant to be lived inside that love, by people who belong to the Lord.

chunks.text: You are God's chosen people, holy and loved. So clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience. Put up with one another. If anyone has a complaint against someone, forgive each other. Forgive as the Lord forgave you.
Above all, live in love, which ties everything together and makes it complete. Let the peace of God rule in your hearts. You were called to this peace as members of one body. And be thankful.

Let the word of Christ live in you richly. Teach and guide one another wisely. Sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs to God with grateful hearts. Whatever you say or do, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.

Wives, be subject to your husbands, as is right for those who belong to the Lord. Husbands, love your wives, and do not be harsh with them. Children, obey your parents in everything, for this pleases the Lord. Fathers, do not provoke your children, so they will not lose heart.

Gospel.box: Forty days after his birth, Mary and Joseph bring Jesus to the Temple in Jerusalem, as the law of Moses asked for a firstborn son. There the old man Simeon and the widow Anna, who had waited all their lives for God's promise, recognize the child as the Savior. The pair of birds was the offering the law allowed for families who could not afford a lamb.

chunks.text: When the time came for their purification under the law of Moses, Mary and Joseph brought Jesus up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord. The law of the Lord says, "Every firstborn son shall be set apart for the Lord." They also came to offer a sacrifice, as the law says: "a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons."

There was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon. He was good and faithful, waiting for God to comfort Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him. The Holy Spirit had shown him that he would not die before he had seen the Messiah sent by the Lord.
Led by the Spirit, Simeon came into the Temple. When the parents brought in the child Jesus to do what the law required, Simeon took him in his arms and praised God, saying:

"Master, now you can let your servant go in peace, as you promised. For my own eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared in the sight of all peoples. He is a light to show the way to the nations, and the glory of your people Israel."

The child's father and mother were amazed at what was said about him. Simeon blessed them and said to Mary, his mother, "This child is set for the fall and the rise of many in Israel. He will be a sign that many will speak against, and a sword will pierce your own soul too. In this way the thoughts of many hearts will be brought to light."

A prophet named Anna was also there. She was the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher, and she was very old. She had been married seven years, and had lived as a widow for many years since. She never left the Temple, but worshiped God night and day with fasting and prayer. Coming up at that very moment, she gave thanks to God and spoke about the child to everyone who was waiting for God to set Jerusalem free.

When Mary and Joseph had done everything the law of the Lord required, they went back to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth. The child grew and became strong. He was filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.

plain.carry: This week I will treat the people at home with the patience and forgiveness Paul describes, and thank God for each of them.

kids.headline: Jesus Had a Family Too
kids.intro: Today we celebrate the Holy Family: Jesus, Mary, and Joseph. Jesus grew up in a home with people who loved him and took care of him. The readings show us how families can love and care for each other.
kids.listen: the two old people in the Temple who had been waiting to meet Jesus

Reading 1.box: A wise teacher named Sirach tells children to honor their mother and father. He says God is pleased when we love our parents and take care of them, even when they get old.

chunks.text: God wants children to respect their fathers and mothers. When you honor your dad, God helps make up for the wrong things you have done. When you honor your mom, it is like saving up treasure. People who honor their parents will be happy with their own children someday, and God will listen when they pray. God will give them a long life. When you listen to God, you make your mother glad.

Take care of your father when he is old, and do not make him sad. If he forgets things or gets confused, be patient with him. Never look down on him. God will never forget the kind things you do for your parents.

Responsorial Psalm.box: This song says people who love God and follow his ways are happy. It pictures a family sitting together around the table, growing strong like young trees.

Reading 2.box: Saint Paul tells the first Christians how to treat each other at home. He says to be kind, to forgive, and most of all to love.

chunks.text: God loves you and has chosen you. So put on kindness, gentleness, and patience the way you put on clothes. If someone hurts you, forgive them, because the Lord forgives you. Most of all, love each other. Let God's peace fill your heart, and always say thank you.
Keep the words of Jesus in your heart. Help each other learn, and sing songs to God together. Whatever you say and whatever you do, do it for Jesus, and thank God the Father.

Paul has a word for each person in the family. He tells wives to follow their husbands' lead, as people who belong to the Lord, and he tells husbands to love their wives and never be harsh with them. Children, obey your parents, because this pleases God. Fathers, do not be so hard on your children that they give up.

Gospel.box: When Jesus was a tiny baby, Mary and Joseph took him to God's house, the Temple, to offer him to God. There they met Simeon and Anna, two old people who had been waiting their whole lives to see the Savior.

chunks.text: Mary and Joseph brought baby Jesus to the Temple in Jerusalem to offer him to God, as God's law said. They also brought two small birds as a gift to God.

A good man named Simeon lived in Jerusalem. He loved God and was waiting for the Savior God had promised. The Holy Spirit had told him he would see the Savior before he died. That day the Spirit led him to the Temple. When he saw Jesus, he took the baby in his arms and praised God.
Simeon prayed, "God, you kept your promise. Now I can go in peace, because I have seen the one who will save us. He is a light for all the people of the world, and the glory of your people Israel."

Mary and Joseph were amazed. Simeon blessed them and said to Mary, "Many people will turn toward this child, and many will turn against him. Because of him, what people really think in their hearts will be shown. And your heart will hurt, as if a sword had pierced it."

An old woman named Anna was there too. She was a prophet who stayed in the Temple day and night, praying to God. Her husband had died long ago. When she saw Jesus, she thanked God and told everyone who was waiting for the Savior about him.
Then Mary, Joseph, and Jesus went home to Nazareth. Jesus grew big and strong and wise, and God's grace was with him.

word.meaning: The Temple was the great house of prayer in Jerusalem where God's people went to worship him.

kids.draw: Draw your family gathered around a table, and give each person a small heart to show one kind thing they do for the family.
kids.ask: What is one way you can show your mom, dad, or the grown-ups who care for you that you love and respect them?

family.opener: Today we celebrate Jesus, Mary, and Joseph, a real family who prayed together, kept God's law, and cared for one another.
questions: How can we take care of the older people in our family, the way Sirach asks?
Which of Paul's words, like kindness, patience, or forgiveness, does our family most need right now?
Simeon and Anna waited many years for God's promise, so what are we waiting for God to do in our family?
family.try: Choose one meal this week to eat together with no screens, and let each person thank someone at the table for something specific.
family.pray: Jesus, Mary, and Joseph, help our family grow in patience, forgiveness, and love, and teach us to welcome Jesus into our home every day.
